member.name: T:BimGo.Audio.WeatherSound
member.summary: Round W-C: the weather's sound: a streamed waveOut channel of its own (opened the first time it's needed) mixing the rain's looping hiss and thunder rumbles, all synthesised at start (no sound files). The game loop calls every frame: each finished buffer is refilled with the next stretch of the mix (about three quarters of a second queued), so the level and the muffling under a roof change smoothly without restarting anything. No allocations after start; failures (no audio device) leave it silent.

Sidecar (Revit sessions): <model>.bimgo-bookmarks.json beside the model, saved on every change.

member.name: T:BimGo.Game.Guns.GizmoController
member.summary:
The move / rotate gizmo shared by the Gizmo and Clone guns.
Locking on starts in : WASD (or the arrows) move the target in plan relative to the view, E raises it and Q lowers it. R switches to : A / D (or ← / →) turn it counter-clockwise / clockwise about its pivot on the XY plane (no other rotations: Revit families stay level). Shift slows either down.
Snap mode (G toggles it; holding Ctrl inverts it for as long as it is held) clamps the change since locking on to the session's increments ( / ): each key press (and key repeat) steps one increment, plan moves follow the world X / Y axis nearest the view direction, so offsets stay exact multiples. Z / X step the current mode's increment down / up. The owning gun decides what committing and cancelling mean.

member.name: F:BimGo.Game.Guns.GizmoController.MAX_DROP
member.summary: Drop to surface: furthest drop (m) below the element's base.

member.name: F:BimGo.Game.Guns.GizmoController.LIFT_REACH
member.summary: Drop to surface: the ray starts this far (m) above the box's base (at most half the box's height), so an element sunk into a floor or desk by up to this much is lifted onto it instead of dropping through.

member.summary: Drops or lifts the target so the bottom of its box rests on the first surface straight below the box's bottom centre: one ray down from above the base (at most half the box's height), against the visible static scene and the other moved / cloned elements, never the target itself. The first hit wins, so a lamp over a desk lands on the desk, not the floor under it. Stays locked on (uncommitted): RMB commits it as an ordinary move.

member.returns: True when the target moved.

member.name: T:BimGo.Game.Guns.GizmoGun
member.summary: Gun 7: move / rotate loadable family instances (FFE). LMB on an eligible element locks the gizmo on in move mode: WASD move it relative to the view, E / Q raise / lower it. R switches to rotate mode: A / D turn it CCW / CW on the XY plane. Shift for fine control. G toggles snapping to fixed increments (Ctrl inverts while held); Z / X step the current mode's increment; F drops (or lifts) it onto the surface below. RMB commits (the same move and rotation are applied in Revit, or recorded in the file); Esc cancels. F while only aiming drops the aimed element and commits at once.

member.name: T:BimGo.Game.Guns.HammerGun
member.summary:
Gun 6: the demolition hammer. LMB primes the element under the crosshair; LMB on a primed element demolishes it in the game and in the model source (Revit, or the file's journal). By default it sets Phase Demolished to the session's "new" phase, which only existing elements (there in the "existing" phase) accept; new work, clones and unphased elements can only be deleted (T toggles to deleting). RMB un-primes, X clears all primes.
Removal is optimistic: the element vanishes at once and comes back if Revit refuses. In a standalone file both modes hide the element and record the mode for a later push to Revit.

member.name: T:BimGo.Game.Guns.MeasureGun
member.summary:
Gun 2: measuring, in four modes (review tools round). Pressing 2 again (while it is the selected gun) cycles Distance → Area → Angle → Clearance. RMB removes the last measurement (or cancels the one being made); X twice clears them all. Round Y-A: measurements are saved (measurements.json in the model folder, or inside the .bimgo on save; / ); I shows / hides them, E exports a CSV.
Distance: LMB start, LMB end, a rubber band in between. N snaps the end along the start face's normal.
Area: LMB adds corners on the plane of the first point (the aim ray meets that plane); clicking the first corner again, or RMB with three or more corners, closes the outline. Shows the area and perimeter.
Angle: three clicks: first arm, vertex, second arm (0–180°).
Clearance: along the aimed surface's normal (Round Y-A). A floor or ceiling: from the aimed point straight down to the surface below and up to the next surface above, both labelled, with the total. A wall (or a steep surface): straight out from it, level, to the next surface across. A live preview follows the crosshair.
Values follow the display units (metric / imperial) chosen in the pause menu.

member.name: T:BimGo.Game.Guns.PlaceGun
member.summary:
Gun 9 (next round): places new instances of loadable family types from the family library.
Not holding anything: LMB opens the library (pause menu panel); RMB places the last picked type again.
A picked type appears in front of the player, resting on the surface below, in the gizmo's move mode (the Clone gun's controls: WASD · E / Q · R rotate · G snap · Z / X steps · F drop to surface).
RMB commits: Revit places the type (live session, one undo step) or the file's journal records a place; Esc discards.
A placement is a clone of the type's hidden template, so once committed every other gun treats it like a clone (Gizmo moves it, Clone copies it, Demolish deletes it).
Round X-B: ENTOURAGE mode (the wheel switches; the default without a family library): billboards. RMB plants the type picked in the ENTOURAGE panel where you aim (or swaps the aimed billboard to it); LMB on a billboard removes it, else opens the panel; Z / X shrink / grow the aimed one, R mirrors it.

member.name: T:BimGo.Game.PathStore
member.summary:
Round K-A: the session's keyframed camera paths, persisted like bookmarks:
Sidecar (Revit sessions): paths.json in the model folder, saved on every change.
Embedded (.bimgo files): kept in memory and saved with the file (paths.json); changes raise so the document can be marked dirty.
Positions are kept in Revit internal metres (like bookmarks); is the scene-local copy. All IO failures are caught and reported via .

member.name: T:BimGo.Game.VideoRecorder
member.summary: Writes a walkthrough video on a worker thread (tour round, build A2). The game thread renders each frame, reads it back into a buffer rented from a small pool, and submits it; the worker encodes it with and hands the buffer back. With every buffer queued, renting waits for the encoder (memory stays at a few frames, even at 4K). Cancelling deletes the file. Never throws to the caller.

member.name: T:BimGo.Native.Gl
member.summary: BimGo's OpenGL facade. Renderer and UI code call Gl.Xxx(...) with the uint constants below; each wrapper forwards to Silk.NET.OpenGL (MIT, pinned in BimGo.App.csproj), casting the constants to . Entry points resolve through (wglGetProcAddress, then the opengl32.dll export for GL 1.1), lazily and once each; forwarding does not allocate. must be called on the game thread with a current context. To use a new GL function: add a wrapper here (and its GL name to ), then call it through the renderer. Context creation stays in .

member.name: T:BimGo.Native.Mp4Writer
member.summary:
H.264 / MP4 writing through Windows Media Foundation's sink writer (tour round, build A2: walkthrough video). Media Foundation is part of Windows (the H.264 encoder is licensed by Microsoft for in-box use): no package, no bundled codec. Hand-written interop: four exported functions and the few COM methods needed, called through their vtable slots (slot numbers checked against the Windows SDK's mfobjects.idl / mfreadwrite.idl).
Frames go in as top-down BGRA (MFVideoFormat_RGB32); the sink writer converts to NV12 for the encoder. Not thread-safe: create, write and finish on one thread (the recorder's worker).

member.name: T:BimGo.Physics.CharacterController
member.summary:
A deterministic capsule controller: gravity, jump, crouch, stair climbing and ground snapping, resolved by iterative depenetration against BVH triangles. Positions are the capsule's feet (bottom). Z is up.
Stairs are climbed in two ways:
Edge riding (most stairs): a contact on the capsule's rounded bottom that sits no higher than above the feet (a nosing, the top of a riser, a kerb, a stringer edge…) lifts the capsule straight up instead of pushing it back, so the round bottom rolls up over the edge like a short ramp. This works whatever the riser looks like (square, sloped, rounded nosings, open risers) and at any walking angle, and needs no separate "am I blocked?" test.
Step-up with look-ahead (risers taller than the capsule's rounded bottom can ride, i.e. a step height setting above ~0.27 m): when blocked, the controller probes a capsule radius ahead at step height and, if there is a floor to land on, lifts the feet to it.
Earlier versions only had the step-up, probing one tick ahead (~3 cm): the round bottom still hung on the nosing, the landing contact read as a wall, and the climb was refused — which is why the step height setting seemed to make no difference.

member.summary: A step edge must sit at least this far below the bottom sphere's centre (else it's a wall).

member.name: T:BimGo.Physics.DynamicInstance

member.name: T:BimGo.Program
member.summary:
BimGo.exe entry point.
Usage: BimGo.exe [model.bimgo] or BimGo.exe --session <id> (what Go in Revit runs). BimGo.exe --kiosk model.bimgo (Round Z-C) opens the file in kiosk mode: visitors walk, fly and look only. Holding Shift while it starts (or --safe) is a safe start: default settings for that run, nothing saved. A second launch hands its file / session to the running instance and exits (a kiosk launch only brings the running window forward). BimGo.exe --register / --unregister add or remove the .bimgo association and the Start-menu shortcut for the current user (add --quiet for no message box), then exit.

member.name: T:BimGo.Rendering.LightShadows
member.summary:
Cached omnidirectional shadow maps for the artificial lights: one depth "cube" (6 faces, 90° each) per light, in a depth texture array of × 6 layers (16-bit, hardware comparison). Works on GL 3.3 (no cube-map arrays): the shaders pick the face from the major axis themselves, with the same face table as / .
Fixtures don't move, so a light's map is rendered once and kept in a slot while the light stays picked. A map is re-rendered when its light moves (gizmo) or the scene changes (hide, demolish, move, category toggle); until then the stale map is still used. At most lights render per frame, never-rendered ones first, nearest first; a light without a map yet is left out and fades in once it has one.
Never throws: failures set (the renderer then lights without shadows).

member.name: T:BimGo.Rendering.MaterialTextures
member.summary:
GPU side of the Realistic colour mode: the material table and the texture images.
Images go into up to four mipmapped RGBA8 texture arrays by size (256², 512², 1024², 2048²). Each image takes the smallest bucket that holds its longest side (never above the size it was extracted at), so a model of 256 px library textures doesn't pay for 1024² layers. Rectangular images are stretched to the square layer; their real-world width and height keep the proportions on screen.
The table is a small RGBA32F texture, six texels per material (read with texelFetch, so any number of materials fits on GL 3.3): t0 (colour, fade) · t1 (image tint, glass reflectivity) · t2 (scale U, scale V, offset U, offset V) · t3 (cos angle, sin angle, bucket or -1, layer) · t4 (appearance tint, flags: 1 = invert the image) · t5 (shine 0–1, roughness 0–1, flags: 1 = metallic, 2 = water; ripple strength). Keep in step with .
Proxies: a material with no embedded image but a proxy keyword () gets the pack's image as one more layer, drawn fully (fade 1, no image tint) at the proxy's real-world size.
One draw path for every material: the scene shader picks the material per vertex, nothing is bound per batch. Images that can't be decoded are left out (the material shows its colour). After a change in the Textures panel, then rebuild everything (the vertex streams stay).

member.name: T:BimGo.Rendering.ReflectionProbes
member.summary:
Reflection probes (reflection probes round, build B): static captures of the model around a point, read by the scene shader for reflective surfaces instead of the sky.
Where: one probe per Revit room that holds a reflective surface (shine tier 25 % + or water), a grid of probes in large rooms (longest side over ), and fallback probes for reflective surfaces outside rooms (outdoor water, unroomed areas), one per cell. Rooms without reflective surfaces get none, so a model without shine bakes nothing.
Storage: six faces per probe (90° each, the light-shadow face table) in one mipmapped RGBA8 texture array (GL 3.3 has no cube-map arrays). Mips are the blur: rough surfaces read a smaller level.
Lookup: a plan grid ( plan cells × height bands, a texture array) holds up to two probes per cell and a blend weight, so a fragment finds its probes with one fetch, and room boundaries blend over about . Each probe's position and room box (for box projection) sit in a small float texture.
Baking: progressive, faces per frame, nearest unbaked probe first, then stale ones (sun, lights, colour mode, edits). Until a probe is baked its cells show the sky. A probe baked while the player was far away (lights and sun shadows are fitted around the player) is refreshed once when the player comes near.
Never throws: GL failures set (the renderer then reflects the sky).

member.name: M:BimGo.Rendering.ReflectionProbes.BuildGrid(BimGo.Scene.SceneData)
member.summary:
The lookup grid over the probes' boxes, built once per placement so nothing here costs per frame (next round: probes no longer leak between rooms).
Rooms per cell: every room, with a probe or not, claims the cells whose centre lies inside its plan, and in height the room whose floor () is the nearest below the cell centre wins. A slab's cells belong to the room above it (the shader looks a ceiling up below it, in the room underneath), and a room without a probe keeps its cells, so no neighbour or fallback probe shows in it.
Probe per cell: the nearest probe of the cell's room (plan distance); cells in no room take the nearest fallback probe whose box holds them.
Blending only through openings: where two probes meet they blend over only if the boundary is open: a short horizontal ray across it hits nothing in the occluder set (doors and movable furniture are left out, see ), or the gap lies inside a door's box. Probes of one large room always blend. Walls get a hard change, which the shader's normal offset keeps on the wall itself.

member.name: M:BimGo.Rendering.ReflectionProbes.AssignRooms(BimGo.Scene.RoomInfo[],System.Int32)
member.summary: The room of every lookup cell (-1 none): the cell centre inside the room's plan, and of the rooms there the one whose floor is the nearest below the centre (within under it, and no more than above its top: Revit rooms often stop below the ceiling). Host rooms win ties.

member.summary: True when the boundary between two neighbouring cells (centres and , same height band) is open: the gap lies in a door's box, or a horizontal ray across it (from a quarter cell before to a quarter cell past ) hits no occluder. The ray runs at the band's height, kept 0.15 m above the higher floor and below the lower top of the two rooms. Without occluders (none set) only doors count as open.

member.name: T:BimGo.Rendering.SceneRenderer
member.summary: Round X-B: billboards (entourage: trees, shrubs, people, cars, the user's own cut-outs). Their pictures are one RGBA texture array (512 px layers, mipmapped, bound to the scratch unit 0 only while they draw); each billboard is one instance of a 4-vertex strip (16 floats: base and height, width / flip / layer / look, colour and luminance scale, the picture's content box). They face the eye in the scene and the sun in the shadow maps (so their shadow is the full silhouette), take the sun, its shadows and the artificial lights, and stay out of AO, probes, the minimap and light shadows.

Owns the static scene buffers and draws sky, batches, ground and highlights, and (when the sun is on) the cascaded shadow maps. Lighting comes from : off = the classic fixed light. Ambient occlusion and the glow (when on) share a half-resolution geometry pre-pass drawn here and processed by . Artificial lights () and emissive surfaces are lit in the scene and ground shaders.

Grass round (build B): grass blades over the grass materials, in the Realistic mode. The grass field (a CPU raster of where grass grows, ) becomes an RG32F texture; each frame two instanced draws (a dense near grid and a sparser far ring with wider blades) place blades from it in the vertex shader. Blades take the sun, its shadows and the artificial lights, but cast no shadows and stay out of AO, probes and pictures of other views (minimap, clash view).

Round Y-D1: occlusion culling of the main view, with GL occlusion queries.
Each frame (main view only: never photos, videos, clash pictures, probes, reflections or shadows), after the opaque scene, the dynamic elements, the section caps and the ground are drawn, every chunk in view that is due () gets an ANY_SAMPLES_PASSED query of its box (grown by ), with colour and depth writes off.
At the start of the next frame the answers that are in decide which chunks the opaque pass, the AO pre-pass and the transparent pass skip. An answer that isn't in yet keeps its chunk drawn: the CPU never waits.
Boxes for every chunk sit in one buffer (36 vertices each, made once), so a query is one draw.
Y-D1 r2: boxes draw their front faces only (half the fill); a cluster of hidden chunks () is queried as one box; Auto culls only while the view holds over triangles (off again under ).
The trade: a chunk that comes into sight from behind a wall shows a frame late (the margin, the near rule and the camera-jump rule hide most of that).
Photo mode (photo round): exposure, a flat multiply over the finished scene in the current target (−2 to +2 EV, the same in the preview and in the photo).

Round X-C1 (after Gavin's first test): planar reflections for glass and mirrors. Screen-space reflections can't show what a pane facing you reflects (it's behind you, off screen), so glass and mirrors get a true mirrored view instead. Stills only since revision 4 (live, panes popped between views as the chosen planes changed): photos, videos, batch stills and photo mode's preview (2 planes there).
Planes (): the model's glass and smooth mirror-like triangles grouped by plane at load (and when the materials change); only walls of glass, not floors (|n.z| < 0.7: floors and water keep SSR).
Each still the planes that look biggest (2, 4 or 8 by quality, within 40 m) are drawn from the camera mirrored in the plane, everything behind the plane cut away (one more clip plane), into a texture array layer at half or full resolution: sky, the opaque scene, ground, billboards, glass. No AO, SSR or planar reflections inside the mirrored view (probes and sky as usual).
The scene shader looks a glass or mirror fragment up in the layer of the plane it lies on, at its own screen position (a point on the plane lands on the same pixel in both views).
Texture unit 19 (a 2D array: one sampler for both planes, so the scene shader stays within 16 samplers).

Round Y-D2: the main view's depth pre-pass. The opaque static scene (with occlusion culling's skips) and the moved / cloned elements are drawn depth-only first ( on , whose gl_Position is invariant); the shaded opaque pass then tests EQUAL with depth writes off, so the expensive per-pixel lighting runs once per pixel instead of once per surface drawn over it (chunks aren't sorted front to back). Not in the clash view or the minimap (their own drawing).

Colour round A: colour profiles. Each vertex carries its element's index (attribute 6, made the first time a profile shows); one RGBA8 texel per element ( a row, unit ) holds the element's colour and code, fetched in the vertex shader. A new profile, or a change to one, rewrites that small texture only: no geometry is touched, so thousands of elements recolour at once. Ghosted elements are left out of the normal passes and drawn by .

Round X-C1: screen-space reflections (Realistic mode). Upward-facing reflective surfaces (water, shiny floors and tops; after Gavin's first test, glass and mirrors use planar reflections instead: see SceneRenderer.PlanarReflections) march their reflected ray through this frame's half-resolution geometry pre-pass (view depth, the one AO and bloom use) and, where it meets a surface on screen, take that surface's colour from the previous frame (reprojected with the previous frame's camera, so the camera may move). Misses (off screen, the sky, behind something) keep the probe or sky reflection, faded in between, so SSR only ever sharpens what was there.
History: the scene target's colour copied after the glass and the weather (before bloom, markers and UI) into a mipmapped texture: rougher surfaces read a blurrier mip.
Quality (): 0 off, 1 low (12 steps), 2 medium (24), 3 high (48), each step further than the last (6 cm to 60 m), then a few halving steps on the hit.
Texture units 17 (pre-pass) and 18 (history): 1–16 are taken. Off for probe captures, the plan minimap and clash pictures (no pre-pass for those).

The section cut (section box round): the scene and geometry pre-pass shaders discard what the cut's planes remove (, passes with ), and fills the cut solids. Shadows, light shadows and reflection probes ignore the cut (the whole building still casts and reflects).
Caps, per plane whose cut-away side holds the eye (the only planes whose caps can face it): (1) the opaque scene cut by that plane alone is drawn into the stencil with INVERT, no colour, no depth test, so a pixel stays odd when its ray, from the plane on, ends inside a solid; (2) the cap polygon (the box face, or a large square on the free plane, cut by the other planes) is drawn where the stencil is odd, depth-tested, in one flat colour (the user's choice). Cost: one extra opaque pass per facing plane (often none when inside the box).

Round W-B: rain and snow. The cover map (: the highest surface over each cell of the site) becomes an R32F texture that the scene, ground and grass shaders read to find surfaces open to the sky (wet, or under snow) and that the falling drops and flakes stop at. The drops and flakes are one instanced draw in a box round the eye (see ), drawn after the glass, depth-tested and blended.

member.name: T:BimGo.Rendering.ScreenEffects
member.summary:
The half-resolution geometry pre-pass and the two screen-space effects fed by it:
Ambient occlusion. The pre-pass writes view-space normal + view depth (RGBA32F); runs the AO pass and a two-pass depth-aware blur, leaving (AO, depth) bound on ; the scene and ground shaders upsample it and darken their ambient (sky) term only.
Glow (bloom). The same pre-pass writes each surface's emissive colour to a second target (RGBA16F), already hidden behind whatever is in front of it. takes it to quarter resolution and blurs it; adds it over the finished scene.
The pre-pass is separate from the (possibly multisampled) scene target, so MSAA and these effects never interact; glass is not in the pre-pass (it neither occludes nor glows).
GL resources are created on first use; until then (and when both effects are off) a 1×1 placeholder keeps the shaders' AO sampler valid. Never throws: failures set and the caller switches off.

member.summary: Texture unit the bloom passes read from (kept off the AO unit, which the scene pass still needs).

member.summary: World-space sampling radius (m): corners, skirting, furniture against walls.

member.name: F:BimGo.Rendering.ScreenEffects.INTENSITY
member.summary: Strength (each tap adds 0..1). 3.5 takes a 90° inside corner to about 0.6 (tuned on a test room).

member.summary: Photo exposure (vertex shader: ): a flat colour blended over the scene with glBlendFunc(DST_COLOR, ZERO) (darker: colour = factor) or (DST_COLOR, ONE) (brighter: colour = factor − 1).

member.name: F:BimGo.Rendering.Shaders.SCENE_VS
member.summary: Scene vertex shader. aEmissive (location 3) is the per-vertex glow (RGB colour, A = strength / 4); models without glowing surfaces leave the attribute disabled, so it reads (0, 0, 0, 1) = no glow. aMaterial (4, the Realistic-mode material index; 65535 = none) and aUv (5, surface coordinates in metres) are only enabled for snapshots with materials; the fragment shader only reads them when uRealistic = 1. Colour round A: aElement (6, the element's index as a float: exact up to 16.7 million) is only enabled once a colour profile was shown; with uProfilePass above 0 the element's profile code is fetched here, once per vertex, from uProfileTex (one RGBA8 texel per element, PROFILE_WIDTH texels a row): rgb = colour, a = code (0 normal, 1 ghost, 2 hidden, 255 coloured).

member.name: F:BimGo.Rendering.Shaders.PROFILE_WIDTH
member.summary: Colour round A: texels per row of the profile texture (keep in step with the GLSL above).

member.name: F:BimGo.Rendering.Shaders.CLOUD_GLSL
member.summary:
Realistic colour mode (inserted after LIGHTS_GLSL in the scene fragment shader). The material table holds six texels per material (MaterialTextures): t0 (colour, fade) t1 (image tint, glass reflectivity) t2 (scale U, scale V, offset U, offset V) t3 (cos angle, sin angle, bucket or -1, layer) t4 (appearance tint, flags; 1 = invert the image, 2 = a proxy whose image tint always multiplies) t5 (shine, roughness, flags: 1 = metal, 2 = water; ripple strength).
Reflections (reflection probes round, build A, sky only): shine is rounded to the nearest 25 % tier and reflects when the tier reaches uReflectThreshold (water always). Each tier is drawn at a fixed head-on strength (metals 0.30 / 0.55 / 0.90, other surfaces half that, Fresnel adds the rest at grazing angles); roughness blurs the sky towards its average and takes away most of the grazing boost. Glass: Revit's value × 2.5, kept within 10–50 %. uReflectGain is the user's strength slider. Water tilts the normal with six travelling waves (uTime: the water clock, which runs at the ripple speed), scaled by uWaterWaves (ripple strength; 0 skips the waves) and stretched by uWaveScale (wave size: the wavelengths × it, the slope unchanged) and faded with distance, and adds a sun glint (no shadow test).
Probes (build B): where the plan grid (uProbeGrid) names a baked probe, the reflection reads it instead of the sky: box-projected against the probe's room box, the mip level from roughness, two probes blended near room boundaries. Faces use the light-shadow face table (FACE_F / FACE_U / LIGHT_PAD from LIGHTS_GLSL, which comes first). uReflectDebug 2 colours each probe's cells. Images live in one array per size bucket; the gradients are taken from the metric coordinates before any branching (textureGrad), so mip selection stays correct inside the per-material branches. Keep the four buckets in step with MaterialTextures.BUCKETS.
Order per fragment: image → invert → image tint → fade over the colour → appearance tint over the result, all in linear light as Revit's renderer does (checked on Gavin's tint test model: a 50 % fade and an inverted image only match Revit's Realistic view when blended linearly). The result goes back to the display-referred values the rest of the lighting expects. Proxies are coloured before linearising (their tint is worked out in display values). uTintMode: 0 = Revit tint off, otherwise multiply (Revit's blend, confirmed on the same model).

member.name: F:BimGo.Rendering.Shaders.SSR_GLSL
member.summary: Round X-C1: screen-space reflections for the scene shader (after MATERIALS_GLSL; see SceneRenderer.ScreenReflections). The reflected ray is marched through this frame's half-resolution pre-pass (camera-basis normal, view depth; 0 = sky) in steps that grow from 6 cm to 60 m; a step that passes behind a surface (within a thickness that grows with the step) is refined by halving, and the hit is looked up in the previous frame's colour through the previous camera. The alpha is how far to trust it: faded at the screen edges, far along the ray, on surfaces facing away from the ray and on rough surfaces (whose blur reads a lower mip). 0 = keep the probe or sky reflection.

member.name: F:BimGo.Rendering.Shaders.PLANAR_GLSL
member.summary: Round X-C1: planar reflections for the scene shader (after SSR_GLSL; see SceneRenderer.PlanarReflections): up to eight glass / mirror planes drawn for a still from the mirrored camera into the layers of uPlanarTex. A fragment lying on one of them (within its slack: the pane's thickness, a second door track, + 3 cm; facing along it) reads the layer at its own screen position.

member.name: F:BimGo.Rendering.Shaders.SUN_GLSL
member.summary: Sun lighting and cascaded shadow lookup, shared by the scene and ground fragment shaders (inserted after the #version line). With uSun = 0 nothing here is evaluated and the classic fixed light is used. Shadow maps: a depth array (hardware comparison, PCF) and a transmittance array (light through glass, already limited to glass in front of the first opaque surface, so it applies to lit receivers only).

member.name: F:BimGo.Rendering.Shaders.AO_GLSL
member.summary: Ambient occlusion lookup, shared by the scene and ground fragment shaders (inserted after SUN_GLSL). uAoMap holds (blurred AO, view depth) at half resolution; the 2×2 half-res texels around the pixel are weighted by bilinear position and by how close their depth is to this fragment's (a joint bilateral upsample), so AO never bleeds across silhouettes. uAoOn = 0 (off, plan view, glass) returns 1.

member.name: F:BimGo.Rendering.Shaders.LIGHTS_GLSL
member.summary: Artificial lights, shared by the scene and ground fragment shaders (inserted after AO_GLSL). Up to 32 point lights picked on the CPU each frame (nearest to the player, in view), each with a cached omnidirectional shadow map (LightShadows: 6 layers per light in one depth array; the face is picked here from the major axis, with the same face table as LightShadows.FaceForward / FaceUp). Light fades to zero at its radius (windowed inverse square); its lobe mixes omnidirectional light with a downward cosine (downlights, panels). A small share of each light also fills what it can see evenly (a stand-in for light bouncing off the floor and walls), darkened by AO, so ceilings and faces turned away aren't black; a third of that fill reaches shadowed spots (under tables), about 2 % of the light through a wall. uLightPos: xyz position, w radius. uLightColor: rgb colour × intensity, w downward share (0–1), or (Round X-D1) below 0 a light profile: -(code + 1), code = slot (5 bits) · aim octahedral u, v (6 bits each) · turn (7 bits), as LightProfiles.Encode packs it; the profile tables are the LightProfiles block (binding 2). uLightShadow: x first layer (-1 = no shadow map), y fade. Keep the 32 in step with ArtificialLighting.MAX_LIGHTS and the constants with LightShadows.

member.name: F:BimGo.Rendering.Shaders.SHADOW_VS
member.summary: Shadow passes: positions through the light matrix (and the instance model), colour for glass.

member.name: F:BimGo.Rendering.Shaders.SHADOW_DEPTH_FS
member.summary: Opaque casters: depth only (colour writes are masked off).

member.name: F:BimGo.Rendering.Shaders.SHADOW_TRANSMIT_FS
member.summary: Glass: multiplies the light that gets through into the transmittance layer (blend ZERO, SRC_COLOR). Transmission = (1 - opacity) x a normalised tint of the material colour, scaled by the Glass slider.

member.name: F:BimGo.Rendering.Shaders.GRASS_VS
member.summary: Grass blades: one instance per blade on a world-anchored grid around the eye (so blades stay put as you walk), placed from the grass map (RG32F: height, palette index + 1; 0 = no grass). Seven vertices per blade (a three-segment tapering strip, bent by its lean and the wind). Blades with no grass under them, behind the eye or past the distance collapse to nothing. A second, sparser grid with wider blades covers the far ring.

member.name: F:BimGo.Rendering.Shaders.GRASS_FS
member.summary: Grass blades' colours: darker at the root, the sun (with shadows), a little light through the blade when looking towards the sun, the artificial lights, fog; both sides lit alike.

member.name: F:BimGo.Rendering.Shaders.BILLBOARD_VS
member.summary: Round X-B: billboards (trees, people, cars…): one instanced quad each, standing on its base and turned about the vertical to face the eye (or, for the shadow maps, the sun: uFaceSun = 1 with uFaceDir the horizontal direction to the sun, so the silhouette casts its full shadow). Per instance: aPos = base xyz, height; aShape = width, flip (±1), picture layer, textured (1) or tinted (0); aTint = colour, 1 / mean luminance; aUv = the picture's content box (u0, v0 top, u1, v1 bottom; the layers are uploaded top row first).

member.name: F:BimGo.Rendering.Shaders.BILLBOARD_FS
member.summary: Round X-B: a billboard's colour: the picture's own (textured) or the category colour shaded by the picture's luminance (tinted); alpha-tested at 0.5. Lit like foliage: the sky (more towards the top), the sun wrapped round (light gets through leaves), its shadows looked up a little towards the sun (past the billboard's own sun-facing caster), the artificial lights, fog.

member.name: F:BimGo.Rendering.Shaders.BILLBOARD_SHADOW_FS
member.summary: Round X-B: a billboard in the sun's shadow maps: depth only, cut out by the picture's alpha.

member.name: F:BimGo.Rendering.Shaders.WEATHER_GLSL
member.summary: Round W-B: the weather block shared by the scene, ground, grass and falling rain / snow shaders. uCoverMap (R32F, nearest) holds the highest surface over each cell of the site (CoverMap); uCoverArea = (min x, min y, cell, 1 = a map), uCoverSize = cells. uWeather = (wet 0–1, snow 0–1, clock (s, puddle ripples), 0); all zero = no weather (one uniform branch). A surface is open to the sky when nothing in its cell (looked up a cell out along its normal, so wall faces read the cell outside the wall) is more than a slope-scaled tolerance above it.

member.name: F:BimGo.Rendering.Shaders.PRECIP_VS
member.summary: Round W-B: falling rain and snow. One instance per drop / flake, in a box round the eye: each has a fixed place in an endlessly repeating world-anchored pattern moving with the fall velocity, wrapped into the box (so drops stay put as you walk). Rain: a thin streak along its velocity, turned to face the eye; snow: a round flake that flutters. Fades towards the box's sides and right at the eye.

member.name: F:BimGo.Rendering.Shaders.PRECIP_FS
member.summary: Round W-B: a drop or flake's colour: nothing under the cover map's surfaces (indoors, under roofs and canopies) or below the ground; a soft streak / disc of uColour at uAlpha.

member.name: F:BimGo.Rendering.Shaders.LENS_VS
member.summary: Round W-C: drops (and melting snowflakes) on the lens. One instance per drop: uDrops[i] = (centre u, v (0–1), radius (a fraction of the frame's height), opacity); uDropShapes[i] = (shape seed, 1 = a snowflake, how far it has melted 0–1, trail length in radii). The quad covers the drop and the trail above it.

member.name: F:BimGo.Rendering.Shaders.LENS_FS
member.summary: Round W-C: a lens drop: a lumpy round lens (a thinner trail above a drop that has slid) showing the scene behind it upside down, magnified and soft, a darker rim and a small highlight. A snowflake starts as a frosted six-armed crystal and melts into a drop.

member.name: F:BimGo.Rendering.Shaders.GEOMETRY_GLSL
member.summary: Geometry pre-pass outputs. 0: the view-space normal (right, up, forward), turned to face the eye, and the view depth (metres along the camera's forward axis); cleared to 0 = nothing there (sky). 1: glow (emissive colour × uGlow, already hidden behind whatever is in front), the bloom's source; only bound when glow is on.

member.name: F:BimGo.Rendering.Shaders.GEOMETRY_FS
member.summary: Geometry pre-pass for scene batches (vertex shader: ). Colour round A: ghosted and hidden profile elements are left out (they don't occlude what is behind them).

member.name: F:BimGo.Rendering.Shaders.DEPTH_PREPASS_FS
member.summary: Round Y-D2: the main view's depth pre-pass (vertex shader: , so depths match the scene pass exactly). Drops exactly what the scene pass's opaque draw drops: section cuts, hidden profile elements and (pass 1) ghosted / see-through coloured ones; colour writes are masked off.

member.name: F:BimGo.Rendering.Shaders.GEOMETRY_GROUND_FS
member.summary: Geometry pre-pass for the ground plane (vertex shader: ).

member.name: F:BimGo.Rendering.Shaders.AO_FS
member.summary: Screen-space ambient obscurance at half resolution (the spiral sampling of McGuire et al.'s SAO with a bounded per-tap estimator). Taps spiral out from the pixel over a world-space radius; each tap's view position is rebuilt from its depth and counts by the cosine of its direction above the surface's tangent plane, fading to nothing at the radius, so each tap adds 0..1 and uIntensity reads directly. A 4×4 ordered rotation per pixel turns banding into fine noise that the 9-tap blur removes. Output: (AO, view depth) for the blur and the upsample.

member.name: F:BimGo.Rendering.Shaders.AO_BLUR_FS
member.summary: Separable depth-aware Gaussian (9 taps along uDir): smooths the AO noise without crossing depth edges.

member.name: F:BimGo.Rendering.Shaders.GLOW_DOWN_FS
member.summary: Bloom: half-resolution glow → quarter resolution, a 4-tap box (bilinear taps cover 4×4 source texels).

member.name: F:BimGo.Rendering.Shaders.GLOW_BLUR_FS
member.summary: Bloom: separable Gaussian at quarter resolution (13 taps along uStep, sigma 4 texels: about 64 screen px wide).

member.name: F:BimGo.Rendering.Shaders.GLOW_COMPOSITE_FS
member.summary: Bloom: added over the finished scene (blend ONE, ONE), bilinear upsampled from quarter resolution.

member.name: F:BimGo.Rendering.Shaders.GRID_VS
member.summary: Grids round A: grid lines and level outlines. Each segment is a quad whose corners share the segment's end point and direction; the vertex shader pushes them sideways to a constant pixel width (screen-facing, like Overlay3D.Line). aAlong is metres along the grid (for the dash-dot pattern; negative = solid, the level outlines).

member.name: F:BimGo.Rendering.Shaders.GRID_FS
member.summary: Grids round A: a Revit-like dash-dot (2.4 m dash, 0.5 m gap, 0.3 m dot, 0.5 m gap) in world metres; once the dot would be under ~3 pixels (far away) the line turns solid so it doesn't shimmer. uDashed 0 (grids round B, the default): solid lines.

member.name: T:BimGo.Rendering.ShadowMaps
member.summary:
Cascaded sun shadow maps: a depth texture array (one layer per cascade, hardware depth comparison) and a matching transmittance array (RGB light let through by glass). Each cascade covers a slice of the camera's view with a bounding sphere, so its size never changes as the view turns, and is snapped to whole texels so edges don't shimmer as the player walks. A cascade is only re-rendered when its matrix, the sun or the scene changes; while walking, the far cascades (big texels, slow to change) refresh every 2nd / 3rd / 4th frame, and the shaders always sample with the matrix each map was actually rendered with ().
GL resources are created on first use; until then (and when shadows are off) 1×1 placeholders keep the shaders' samplers valid. Never throws: failures switch shadows off and set .

member.name: T:BimGo.Shell.AppInstance
member.summary:
Keeps BimGo.exe single-instance. The first instance owns a named mutex and an inbox folder (%LocalAppData%\BimGo\App\inbox); a second instance (e.g. double-clicking another .bimgo, or Revit's "open in BimGo") drops an open request there, brings the first window forward and exits.
Requests are plain JSON files: { "open": "C:\\path\\model.bimgo" } or { "attach": "<sessionId>" } (Go in Revit). Only existing .bimgo paths and well-formed session ids with a session folder are accepted, and nothing in a request is ever executed.

member.name: M:BimGo.Shell.AppInstance.TakeRequest

member.name: T:BimGo.Shell.AppShell
member.summary:
The app: one window that alternates between the home screen and walkthroughs, all on the main thread. A walkthrough runs on a .bimgo file (edits go to its journal) or on a live Revit session (edits go to Revit).
Closing the window quits (after any unsaved-changes prompt); Close model returns to the home screen. While walking: dropped / double-clicked files are queued until the model is closed; a Go from Revit asks before switching; a new snapshot of the current live session reloads where the player stands.

member.name: T:BimGo.Shell.FileAssociation
member.summary:
Registers BimGo for the current user, no admin rights needed: the .bimgo file association (double-click opens in BimGo, with the ">>" icon) under HKCU\Software\Classes, and a Start-menu shortcut.
BimGo.exe --register / --unregister do it on demand. Otherwise the installed copy (%LocalAppData%\Programs\BimGo\BimGo.exe, where the build and the add-ins put it) registers itself quietly on start when the association is missing or points elsewhere, unless the user unregistered. Copies run from elsewhere (a dev build) never register themselves. Never throws.
